jurisdiction.name: International Organization of Securities Commissions
jurisdiction.overview: Official documents of this organisation are listed on its own page and are not counted in member countries' totals.

narrative.summary: IOSCO's Board issued non-binding guidance in 2021 on the use of AI and machine learning by market intermediaries and asset managers, built around six measures on governance, testing, skills, third parties, disclosure and data quality. After a 2025 consultation on AI use cases, risks and challenges in capital markets, it published in May 2026 a non-binding Supervisory Toolkit for AI Use in Capital Markets to help securities regulators supervise firms' AI use.
lead_institutions: IOSCO Fintech Task Force / AI Working Group

instruments.official_title: The use of artificial intelligence and machine learning by market intermediaries and asset managers: Final Report (FR06/2021)
instruments.english_title: The use of artificial intelligence and machine learning by market intermediaries and asset managers
instruments.issuing_authority: Board of the International Organization of Securities Commissions
instruments.publisher_name: Board of the International Organization of Securities Commissions
instruments.summary: Guidance for securities regulators on the use of AI and machine learning by market intermediaries and asset managers, set out as six measures: senior management oversight and a documented governance framework; testing and continuous monitoring of algorithms; adequate staff expertise; management of third-party providers; meaningful disclosure to clients and regulators; and controls for data quality and bias.
instruments.current_status: Final report of the IOSCO Board, published September 2021. IOSCO states the guidance is not binding; members are encouraged to consider it within their legal and regulatory frameworks.
instruments.evidence_reference: Printed date 'September 2021' and non-binding wording read from PDF; only month printed. Consultation predecessor CR02/2020 known from discovery, not re-opened (search budget exhausted).

instruments.official_title: Artificial Intelligence in Capital Markets: Use Cases, Risks, and Challenges – Consultation Report (CR/01/2025)
instruments.english_title: Artificial Intelligence in Capital Markets: Use Cases, Risks, and Challenges
instruments.issuing_authority: Board of the International Organization of Securities Commissions
instruments.publisher_name: Board of the International Organization of Securities Commissions
instruments.summary: Consultation report describing how market participants use AI, including generative AI, in capital markets, the risks and challenges this raises for investor protection, market integrity and financial stability, and the responses of regulators so far. It sought views to inform IOSCO's further policy work on AI.
instruments.current_status: Published by the IOSCO Board in March 2025 for comment until 11 April 2025.
instruments.evidence_reference: Report number CR/01/2025 (Board/2025/017), printed date March 2025 and deadline 11 April 2025 read from PDF. No final version of this specific report identified; the 2026 Supervisory Toolkit is the follow-up output but does not say it finalises CR/01/2025.

instruments.official_title: Supervisory Toolkit for AI Use in Capital Markets: Final Report (FR/02/2026)
instruments.english_title: Supervisory Toolkit for AI Use in Capital Markets
instruments.issuing_authority: Board of the International Organization of Securities Commissions
instruments.publisher_name: Board of the International Organization of Securities Commissions
instruments.summary: Toolkit for securities regulators supervising firms' use of AI. It sets out areas where AI use may warrant closer supervisory attention; tools with sample supervisory questions for governance and risk management, third-party and outsourcing risk, disclosure, and recordkeeping and reporting; and indicators and data sources such as inspections, surveys, supervisory dialogue and data requests. A standalone version of the toolkit (OR/07/2026) was published alongside.
instruments.current_status: Final report of the IOSCO Board, published 25 May 2026. IOSCO describes the tools as practical, non-binding and non-prescriptive.
instruments.evidence_reference: Date 25 May 2026 from IOSCO Public Reports listing; PDF printed 'May 2026'. Non-binding wording from PDF. Standalone toolkit OR/07/2026 (IOSCOPD822.pdf), same date, treated as part of this record.

membership_note: IOSCO's ordinary members are national securities regulators, not governments; the list shows the countries whose regulators are ordinary members. Regulators of territories (such as Hong Kong, Chinese Taipei, Bermuda, Jersey or the Cayman Islands) and the two regional regulators for Central and West Africa are also members but are not listed as countries; associate and affiliate members are not included.

members_source.comment: Ordinary members page lists 134 entries by jurisdiction (some countries have several regulators; Canada is represented by provincial regulators of Alberta, British Columbia, Ontario and Quebec; Bosnia and Herzegovina by the Federation and Republika Srpska regulators; the UAE by federal, Abu Dhabi and DIFC regulators). No date on page; read 2026-10-21.
